 Hon'Ble Anish Kumar Gupta, J. 
1.

Heard Sri Sushil Kumar Tewari, learned counsel for the applicants, Sri Alok Singh Chandel,
Advocate holding brief of Sri Pradeed Kumar Vishnoi, learned counsel for opposite party no.2 and
Ms. Harshita Rani, learned Aga for the State.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking quashing of the entire proceedings of Sessions Trial No. 574 of 2019 (arising out of Case Crime No. 164 of 2019) Under Sections 363, 366, 376D IPC and Sections 5/6 of Protection of Child from Sexual Offence Act, P.S. Bilari, District Moradabad,
pending in the court of learned Special Judge (POCSO Act)-III, Moradabad.

entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 3. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that the instant FIR was lodged by the opposite party no.2 who is the brother of the wife of applicant no.1.
Subsequent to lodging of the FIR, the matter was investigated and the charge sheet was filed on 01.08.2019.

It is stated by learned counsel for the applicants that prior to filing of the charge sheet in the instant case, the parties have already settled their disputes amicably and the marriage of the sister of opposite party no.2 was solemnized with applicant no.1 in accordance with muslim rites and customs with consent of the opposite party no.2 on 06.10.2019.
Since then the applicant no.1 is residing with his wife and out of the said wedlock two children have already born.

After submission of the charge sheet, the applicants filed the instant application seeking quashing of the entire proceeding of the instant case pointing out the aforesaid facts that the parties have settled their disputes amicably.
Having regard to the aforesaid vide order dated 07.04.2023, the parties were directed to appear before the trial court concerned for verification of the said compromise.

Learned counsel for the applicants further submits that as per the aforesaid direction the parties appeared before the trial court on 18.04.2023 for verification of the said compromise, which has been verified by the trial court concerned vide order dated 18.04.2023.
A report in this regard dated 03.05.2023 has been received from the trial court along with the copy of the order verifying the compromise and the compromise arrived at between the parties.

Thus learned counsel for the applicants submits that since the parties have settled their disputes long back even prior to the submission of the charge sheet in the instant case and they are living happily wedded life and out of the said wedlock to children have already born and the applicant no.1 and his wife both are taking care of the children.
Thus in the light of the aforesaid settlement, learned counsel for the applicants seeks quashing of the entire proceeding against the applicants.

4. Learned counsel for the opposite party no.2 does not dispute the aforesaid facts and admits that even prior to the submission of charge sheet the marriage of her sister was solemnized with the applicant no.1, they are married and are living happy married life and out of the said wedlock, two children have already born.

He admits the execution of compromise and subsequent thereto verification thereof, thus he supports the prayer made by learned counsel for the applicants for quashing of the entire proceeding in the instant case.

5. Per contra, learned AGA submits that since the offences under Section 376 as well as 5/6 POCSO Act are involved, which are serious in nature, therefore, the proceedings of the instant case cannot Mazid Alias Suban Khan And Another vs State Of U.P. And Another on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/155836459/
2 be quashed on the basis of compromise arrived at between the parties.
6. Having heard the rival submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court has carefully gone through the record of the case.

sentences.text: From the record of the case, it is apparent that the sister of opposite party no.2 had initially eloped with the applicant no.1 and when she returned back

,
the instant FIR was lodged by the opposite party no.2 making out the allegations of kidnapping,
abduction, rape and also under the provisions of POCSO Act.
On the date of incident as per the educational record, the age of the wife of applicant no.1 herein was 17 years and 8 months.

However,
there is no quarrel between the parties that there is no apprehension in the muslim law with regard to solemnization of the marriage of a girl child even prior to 18 years of her age and just one month after registration of the FIR, the marriage of sister of the opposite party no.2 was solemnized with the applicant no,1 herein as per the muslim rites and customs and they are living happy married life.
Out of the said wedlock, two children have born.

7. Thus, looking at the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears that the instant FIR was lodged by the opposite party no.2 to safe his reputation at the given point of time and subsequently that the marriage of applicant no.1 with the sister of the opposite party no.2, all the parties have condoned the acts done by the applicant no.1 against the sister of the opposite party no.2.
Even the sister of opposite party no.2 has also condoned act and she leads happy life with the applicant no.1.
More than six years of such marriage have passed, parties have settled all their disputes amicably and there is no complaint against each other during the aforesaid period of six years of marriage.

8. Thus looking at the totality of the facts and circumstances of the instant case and in the interest of justice, though technically the offence is made out in the instant case under the provisions of the POCSO Act and Section 376 IPC but subsequent thereto he married with the opposite party no.2 and out of the said wedlock, the two children have already born, thus in the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court finds that continuation of the instant proceedings against the applicants would be nothing but an injustice to the applicants and also the victim and their children as well.

9. In view of the aforesaid, the instant application is allowed in the interest of justice and the entire proceedings of Sessions Trial No. 574 of 2019 (arising out of Case Crime No. 164 of 2019) Under Sections 363, 366, 376D IPC and Sections 5/6 of Protection of Child from Sexual Offence Act, P.S.
Bilari, District Moradabad, pending in the court of learned Special Judge (POCSO Act)-III,
Moradabad, are hereby quashed in view of the subsequent developments and compromise arrived at between the parties.
(Anish Kumar Gupta,J.) November 6, 2025 Ashish Pd.
